releases.name: Release v1.6.1
releases.body:
# Newton v1.6.1

Newton v1.6.1 is a patch release following v1.6.0, focused on simulation setup performance, collision robustness, and viewer compatibility.

For the complete list of changes, see the [changelog](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/v1.6.1/CHANGELOG.md#161---2026-10-05).

## Highlights

- **Faster many-world setup.** Model replication and finalization are faster, with lower collision-filter memory usage for large replicated scenes. (#4159, #4229)
- **Faster deformable simulation.** CUDA VBD and soft-contact processing improve throughput, especially in scenes with many shapes or worlds. (#3995)
- **RTX viewer compatibility.** Support the OVStage runtime interface with OVRTX 0.4 and newer while retaining OVRTX 0.3 compatibility; debug markers, arrows, and custom meshes update correctly after the first frame. (#4256, #4234)
- **Broader USD support.** Allow usd-core 26.08 and usd-exchange 3.x, including Python 3.13 on aarch64. (#4022)
- **More reliable state output and rendering.** MuJoCo rejects disabled-sensor requests that would return stale accelerations or forces, and Viser renders textured meshes without unintended darkening. (#4131, #4223)
- **Configurable ADMM contact storage.** Experimental coupled ADMM adds optional triangle-pair and contact-reduction capacity controls while preserving default allocations. (#4309)

## Notes

Existing call signatures remain compatible with v1.6.0, but some workflows need attention:

- Reacquire retained list-valued `ModelBuilder` attributes after `replicate()` before reading or mutating them.
- Re-test numerical and contact-overflow baselines. Rebuild CUDA tiled VBD solvers after changing triangle or edge stiffness.
- Built-in broad phases always exclude same-body and static-static pairs when body metadata is supplied, even with `include_static_kinematic_pairs=True`. Expert callers requiring unfiltered pairs can omit `shape_body` when calling the broad phase directly.
- With MuJoCo sensors disabled, stop requesting `body_qdd` and `body_parent_f`, or enable sensors.
- OVRTX 0.5.0.377615 with OVStage 0.2.0.377349 has a known CUDA transform-update rendering issue. Use the retained OVRTX 0.3 path for affected scenes. (#4283)

## Acknowledgments

Thanks to @rebeccazhang0707 for the ADMM contact-storage controls, a contribution from outside the Newton maintainer and project-member groups.

releases.name: Release v1.6.0
releases.body:
# Newton v1.6.0

Newton v1.6.0 is a feature release following v1.5.1. It improves collision performance and scheduling, expands OpenUSD-authored particle and deformable workflows, adds graph-friendly robot controllers, introduces compliant mechanics and reusable rod modeling, and broadens the capabilities of the experimental Kamino solver.

For the complete list of changes, see the [changelog](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/v1.6.0/CHANGELOG.md#160---2026-09-10).

## Highlights

- **Faster, configurable collision detection.** CUDA collision work is faster across broad-phase, narrow-phase, and deterministic contact processing. Solvers can schedule rigid and soft self-contact detection, while opt-in predictive contacts help reduce tunneling between checks. (#4063, #3828, #3854)

- **OpenUSD particles and surface extraction.** Newton can import authored MPM particles, materials, and scene configuration from USD and align supported deformable assets with the updated AOUSD proposal. The new `ParticleSurface` workflow turns particle simulations such as fluids into compact meshes for visualization and export, including multi-world and CUDA-graph use cases. (#3869, #3988, #3349)

- **Experimental: graph-friendly robot control.** New Differential IK and operational-space controllers support heterogeneous robot batches, joint-limit and null-space control, and hybrid force/motion tasks. Implicit actuator response, faster CUDA forward kinematics, and explicit actuator-state copying make more control loops reusable inside CUDA graphs. (#4129, #4105, #3855, #3395, #4101)

- **Compliant robots, rods, and mechanisms.** An opt-in compliant ALM mode for `SolverVBD` covers contacts, structural joints, drives, and limits. The new `newton.Rod` type provides validated, reusable inputs for ordered chains and explicit graphs, with material properties or section rigidities converted into local joint stiffness. (#3769, #4009)

- **Experimental: more capable Kamino simulation.** `SolverKamino` adds Coulomb joint friction, joint effort limits, body motion roles, device-resident per-world solve status, and broader batched kinematics support, making multi-world robot simulations easier to configure and diagnose. (#3966, #3990, #3937, #3916)

## Performance improvements

- **Faster startup and replicated MuJoCo setup.** Cold example-load benchmarks improved by 13% to 20% on tested x86 and ARM systems. Across 8,192-world Ant, Cartpole, G1, and Humanoid workloads, MuJoCo solver initialization was 44% to 77% faster; 256-world G1 and Humanoid setup improved by 12% to 22%. (#3839, #3825, #4119)

- **Faster, lighter model finalization.** Shape-BVH construction now uses tiled CUDA reductions for meshes and Gaussian splats; in a measured 4,096-environment rough-terrain workload, this reduced BVH build time from about 903 ms to 17 ms. On ARM, model-initialization CPU memory also fell by 14% for G1 and 25% for Humanoid. (#4001)

- **Faster collision-heavy simulation.** Cross-platform benchmarks measured hydroelastic contact simulation 33% to 37% faster, SDF contact simulation 9% to 23% faster, and pyramid contact simulation 11% to 14% faster. CUDA collision detection, mesh preprocessing, convex support queries, heightfield traversal, and deterministic contact processing all perform less work while preserving contact results. (#4063, #3801, #3961)

- **Lower overhead and memory at scale.** A 64-world hydroelastic workload reduced GPU buffer use from about 54.5 GiB to 3.75 GB while preserving all expected contacts. The tested 8,192-world G1 workloads also spent 30% to 40% less time in Newton-side simulation overhead, and forward kinematics now runs across articulation joints in parallel on CUDA. (#4040, #3395)

## Announcements

### Upgrade attention

- **Joint position-target layout.** `newton.use_coord_layout_targets` now defaults to `True`, so `joint_target_q` has one entry per joint coordinate and matches `joint_q`. Index it with `Model.joint_target_q_start`; set the flag to `False` before building models only as a temporary compatibility path. (#4096)

- **Collision behavior.** Mesh SDF construction now filters fully concave manifold edges by default; pass `edge_concave_filter=False` to retain the previous contact set. Hydroelastic contacts now use margin for interaction distance and gap for detection slack, and XPBD restitution is solved per contact manifold, so re-test scenes tuned around the previous behavior. (#4171, #3719, #4103)

- **USD deformable and cable assets.** The importer adopts the newer AOUSD deformable proposal, including geometry-owned typed thickness and mass arrays, structural stiffness values, and new fallback values. Author array values together with their `elementType`, move thickness to simulation geometry, and re-test assets with unauthored thickness or uneven cable sampling. (#3988, #3730)

### Breaking changes and removals

- **Keyword-only options.** Optional arguments across mature builder, geometry, contact, solver, and selection APIs that were deprecated as positional in v1.4.0 must now be passed by keyword. (#4070)

- **Mesh adjacency.** The deprecated `MeshAdjacency.indices`, dict-based `edges`, `MeshAdjacency.Edge`, and `add_edge()` APIs are removed. Use `tri_indices`, `edge_indices`, and `edge_tri_indices`. (#4110)

- **Joint impedance controllers.** Deprecated index-port overrides and legacy model-free size arguments are removed. Bind indexed array views directly through the controller's resolved coordinate and DOF indices. (#3979)

- **Solver compatibility APIs.** The deprecated `Model.mujoco.dof_passive_damping` alias and VBD `dahl_defaults_enabled` parameter are removed. Use `Model.joint_damping` and explicitly author positive `vbd:dahl_eps_max` and `vbd:dahl_tau` values where Dahl rod friction is required. (#3623, #4024)

### New deprecations and upcoming removals

- **Rod and cable construction.** Migrate from `JointType.CABLE`, `add_joint_cable()`, positional `add_rod()`, `add_rod_graph()`, `CableStiffness`, and the cable-construction helpers to `JointType.ROD`, `add_joint_rod()`, `newton.Rod`, and `ModelBuilder.add_rod(rod=...)`. The old forms remain functional through 1.6 and are eligible for removal in 1.7. (#4009)

- **VBD compliant constraints.** Adopt the compliant ALM path with `rigid_compliant_alm=True` and finite authored stiffness. Pass `False` explicitly only while migrating from the deprecated legacy hard/soft constraint controls; the default will change to `True`. (#3769)

- **Collision ranges and scheduling.** Migrate legacy VBD contact-range and detection-interval names to `soft_contact_gap`, `particle_self_contact_margin` plus `particle_self_contact_gap`, and solver-owned collision schedules. (#3828)

- **Experimental actuator terminology.** Migrate the experimental actuator `Controller*` classes and `controller*` fields to `Drive*` and `drive*`, use `ClampingBase`, and use `ComponentKind.DRIVE`. The former names continue to warn during the 1.6 deprecation window. (#4054)

See the changelog for the complete set of new deprecations, including USD deformable attributes and keyword-only migrations for `Mesh`, `TetMesh`, and `newton.usd.get_mesh()`.

## Dependency updates

- Newton now requires `warp-lang>=1.17.0`.

- The `sim` extra moves to MuJoCo and MuJoCo Warp 3.12.

- USD import workflows require `newton-usd-schemas>=0.5.0`.

- The `onnx` extra moves to `warp-nn[onnx]==0.3.1`, and documentation and example workflows require GitPython 3.1.58 or newer.

No new required dependency names were added. For complete dependency details, see the [`pyproject.toml` comparison](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/compare/v1.5.1...v1.6.0?diff=split).

## Acknowledgments

Thanks to the [Newton Project Members](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton-governance/blob/main/CONTRIBUTORS.md) and to the following contributors from outside the Newton maintainer, TSC, and project-member groups:

- @han-xudong for MJCF actuator and tendon import improvements, Kamino terminal status, triangle-metadata correctness, and the asRoBallet control example. (#3669, #3684, #3685, #3744, #3746, #3937, #3956)

- @ooctipus for predictive rigid contacts, OpenUSD texture-transform preservation, and corrected floating-base IK Jacobians. (#3854, #4007, #4088)

- @ruziniuuuuu for USD collider-approximation handling, mesh-normal input support, and avoiding unused initialization contacts in MuJoCo. (#3831, #3833, #3825)

- @deepspace28 for restoring MuJoCo line-search performance on large models and keeping VBD proxy reaction forces within configured contact capacity. (#3908, #4004)

- @rakhimovv for bounded headless ViewerGL execution, headless-rendering guidance, and VBD edge/face contact validation. (#3930, #3932, #4060)

- @aneangel for Gaussian-splat rendering and stable plane grids in ViewerViser, plus clearer MuJoCo free-joint drive warnings. (#4018, #4019, #4083)

- @LuckyIYI for reducing unnecessary broad-phase work around infinite planes. (#3867)

- @CharlesKZW and @Double7sBurger for MJCF heightfield orientation and heightfield-contact correctness fixes. (#3898, #4005)

- @CoffeeDrivenCoder for supporting non-`int32` mesh indices in normal computation, @sparkle2820 for restoring Python 3.10 `ModelBuilder` construction, and @zlong-911 for NumPy 1.x compatibility in anisotropic Style3D cloth. (#3986, #3942, #4027)

- @liorbenhorin for OpenCV pinhole camera-ray generation and @mcrowleyNV for the mobile documentation navigation fix. (#3901, #4082)

releases.name: Release v1.5.2
releases.body:
# Newton v1.5.2

Newton v1.5.2 is a patch release following v1.5.1. It adds a state-copy helper for stateful actuators used in CUDA graph capture.

For the complete list of changes, see the [changelog](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/v1.5.2/CHANGELOG.md#152---2026-09-09).

## Highlights

- **State preservation across odd-length CUDA graph replays.** The new `Actuator.State.assign()` method lets callers copy advanced actuator state back into existing state buffers at a captured-region boundary. This allows repeated odd-length regions to preserve state while using a single captured graph. The documented alternating-graph pattern remains available as a zero-copy option. ([#4101](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/pull/4101))

## Notes

This release is intended to be API-compatible with Newton v1.5.1. No breaking changes are expected.
